newsitem.title: USA: Merrill adds to public finance for Northeast.
newsitem.headline: Merrill adds to public finance for Northeast.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co has added two veteran bankers to its public finance department to bolster its efforts in the Northeast, a spokesman for the firm said Wednesday.

Frank McKenna, formerly of Raymond James & Asscociates, has joined the New York office of Merrill Lynch as a managing director and will focus on issuers in New York State and assist when needed on New York City, said Dan Alfaro, the Merrill Lynch spokesman.
New York City by itself is one of the nation's top municipal bond issuers.

McKenna specializes in Northeast issuers, especially in New York State, and has worked at a number of firms with northeast municipal bond expertise, including Roosevelt & Cross Inc and Citicorp Securities.

Also joining Merrill Lynch's public finance department in New York is Matthew Deane, formerly a managing director in Reinoso & Co.'s public finance department. Deane will become a managing director and will focus on Massachusetts issuers as well as state revolving loan funds and infrastructure projects, Alfaro said.

The hires are replacements for recent banking defections. Marianne Kozlowski, who covered New York, New Jersey and Massachusetts, and Sonia Toledo, who focused on New York City, recently resigned from the firm. Toledo joined Lehman Brothers. Kozlowski could not be reached for comment.
Merrill Lynch will hire a public finance banker specializing in New York City, said Alfaro.
